howItWorks.title: How it works in 3 simple steps
howItWorks.subtitle: A transparent, accountable bridge from surplus food to local plates.
howItWorks.step1Desc: A donor enters what is available, portion quantity, and the safe consumption window in 60 seconds. AI automatically screens for safety and prohibited policies.
howItWorks.step2Desc: Only approved NGOs, orphanages, and registered community kitchens can claim surplus food batches with real-time push alerts and verification PIN codes.
howItWorks.step3Desc: A voluntary courier or shelter representative collects the food, verifies temperature safety, and confirms delivery, recording transparent public ledger data.
howItWorks.guaranteeDesc: Every charity on FoodLink is verified using government credentials (NGO Darpan ID, Trust Registration, or municipal sanitation certificates) before claiming meals.
howItWorks.samaritanDesc: Surplus meals are handled in accordance with Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) guidelines, with temperature monitoring during courier transit.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.subtitle: Answers to common questions about donation guidelines, shelter organization verification, and Good Samaritan food safety standards.
faq.emergencyDesc: Our coordination desk assists banquet managers, wedding caterers, and shelters with immediate surplus dispatch.
faq.q1: Who can donate food through FoodLink?
faq.a1: Restaurants, wedding halls, banquet caterers, and corporate dining facilities with surplus unserved food can post listings. All donations must be unserved and packed in food-grade containers.
faq.q2: Who is eligible to claim food donations?
faq.a2: Only verified organizations can claim surplus batches. This includes registered NGOs, orphanages, elder care homes, and certified community kitchens verified through official credentials like NGO Darpan or trust registration.
faq.q3: How does FoodLink verify food safety?
faq.a3: Donors state the prepared time and the safe consumption window (hot meals must be consumed within 4 hours). Receiving shelters inspect container integrity and temperature before confirming delivery.
faq.q4: Can individual volunteers help with pickup and delivery?
faq.a4: Yes. Citizens can register as Volunteer Couriers with valid identity proof to transport food packages between donors and nearby shelters using bikes, autos, or vans.
faq.q5: Are there any platform or transaction fees?
faq.a5: No. FoodLink is completely free to use for both donors and receiving charities. Donors also receive verified 80G tax receipts and CSR impact records.
